title: 'Cannot behave like an Indian': HC raps Imran Khan; asks govt to be 'magnanimous'
content: Imran Khan, a US citizen and OCI card holder, faced a Leave India Notice from the Centre. The Bombay high court granted him interim relief after he submitted an unconditional apology. The court clarified that OCI holders don't have the same rights as Indian citizens, particularly regarding protests. Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh argued that the Centre has the power to expel foreigners.

title: Andhra school chainsaw attack: Accused may lose right leg after police encounter
content: Hemanth is facing possible amputation of his right leg due to severe gunshot injuries sustained during a police encounter. He was involved in a chainsaw attack on two minor students at a school in Raptadu. After fleeing, he was located by police who shot at him during a confrontation. One injured student has undergone complex surgeries and is recovering in a hospital in Bengaluru.

title: Pressured for same-sex marriage, 15-year-old school girl dies by suicide
content: A 15-year-old Class 10 student died by suicide at her home on Rahon Road on October 31. Her family has alleged that a 25-year-old woman pressured her for a same-sex marriage through Instagram. The girl's father reported that this pressure caused severe mental stress for his daughter. Police have registered a case against the accused, who has been arrested as part of the ongoing investigation.

title: 'NCP united under Sunetra': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
content: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

title: Google seeks $6.7B in bond sale after $500B wipeout amid AI spending fears
content: Google parent Alphabet is initiating a bond sale in response to a significant market value decline. The company is targeting $6.7 billion through €6 billion in debt offerings. Investors have expressed concerns about the costs associated with expanding artificial intelligence infrastructure. Despite these worries, demand for the new bonds has reportedly exceeded €17 billion.

title: Louisiana family's bid to overturn 30-year-old inheritance ruling fails
content: A Louisiana man died without a will in 1956, and a court recognised his daughter as the heir to his estate in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, another family challenged her right to inherit a 50% share of a property. On October 30, the Louisiana Supreme Court rejected the challenge as legally time-barred, upholding the earlier inheritance ruling.

title: 9 wickets before IND A call-up! Harsh Dubey scripts history with stunning Ranji spell
content: In a stunning display of skill, Harsh Dubey grabbed nine wickets in a Ranji Trophy clash against Madhya Pradesh, setting a new record for Vidarbha. This remarkable achievement came before he got a spot on India's 15-member squad for the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup. Having already made his One Day International debut this year, Dubey firmly establishes himself as a promising all-rounder in Indian cricket.

title: New Zealand couple build castle with secret dungeon on NZ$122,500 land
content: After three decades of craftsmanship, Denise and Greg Powell are parting ways with their extraordinary recycled-brick castle in Broad Bay. What began as a straightforward home evolved into a medieval masterpiece, complete with a secret trapdoor and various salvaged architectural details. As they downsize to a cozier residence nearby, this unique property has seen its value soar since their acquisition in the early 90s.

title: Unable to afford UK home, couple buy French hamlet for £26,000
content: Yip Ward and Paul Mappley went from living in a caravan in England to owning an abandoned French hamlet. The couple bought the property for £26,000, which includes seven cottages, two barns and other buildings. By carrying out much of the restoration themselves, they estimate they have saved more than £100,000 while bringing the historic hamlet back to life.

title: Alex Karp buys 37,000 acres of Swedish forest for $22M; why hunters are barred
content: Alex Karp acquired 15,000 hectares of forest land in Härjedalen, Sweden, through his company Cladonia Skog AB. The purchase was confirmed by Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget, which previously owned the forest land. Hunters in the area received notification about the termination of their leasing agreements after the sale. A representative from Cladonia expressed commitment to preserving the natural landscape and its habitats.

title: Scientists find Serbian mineral almost identical to Superman's kryptonite
content: Scientists discovered a rare white mineral called Jadarite in Serbia in 2004, later finding that its chemical composition closely matched Superman's fictional Kryptonite. Unlike the glowing green substance, Jadarite is neither green nor radioactive. New research suggests the mineral could supply a significant portion of Europe's lithium needs for electric vehicles, although local opposition has prevented mining operations.

title: Injecting to crush kilos: The rise of ‘Mounjaro’ brides
content: Increasingly, couples in India turn to prescription weight-loss medicines to enhance their appearance before weddings. Clinics in cities like Lucknow report a significant rise in inquiries about these medications. Many individuals seek rapid results to boost confidence for their special day, despite potential health risks. Medical professionals highlight the importance of eligibility criteria and caution against misuse of these drugs.

title: Chiefs linked to $15M WR trade as Tyreek Hill return questions persist
content: The Kansas City Chiefs are in a critical evaluation phase as they look into trading wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. just ahead of the deadline. A recent loss to the Denver Broncos highlighted issues in their passing game, prompting the team to consider changes. While Thomas's varying performance raises questions, it also provides a chance for reinvention.

title: Cuba's hospitals on the brink as US sanctions and oil crisis cripple healthcare
content: Cuba's healthcare landscape is facing serious challenges, as critical medical supplies and equipment run dangerously low. Virtually paralyzed, doctors find it increasingly difficult to deliver effective patient care, with vulnerable groups like malnourished infants and life support-dependent patients at great risk during power outages. The Cuban government recognizes its involvement in this crisis, mainly attributing external issues to US sanctions.

title: Delhi's vehicle ban faces its biggest test at borders: Can enforcement keep up?
content: Delhi is set to implement restrictions on older vehicles that fail to meet BS6 emission standards from entering the city. However, officials are grappling with the difficulty of monitoring numerous entry points, especially during rush hours. Leveraging technology, such as automatic number plate recognition, will be essential for identifying non-compliant vehicles. Collaboration between Delhi and neighboring NCR states is vital to prevent alternative routes and ensure effective enforcement.

title: 'Why should I wake up at 5 am?': Sarfaraz Khan opens up on India snubs & motivation
content: Sarfaraz Khan remains motivated to play cricket despite being overlooked for national selection multiple times. He questions his daily efforts while seeking inspiration from his father's dedication to his career. Although he has performed well in domestic matches, the selector's perception limits his opportunities for overseas play. Sarfaraz's focus on fitness has resulted in significant weight loss and improved performance.

title: ACT: Dilpreet scores brace as India thrash Korea 8-0 to finish league stage unbeaten
content: India thrashed South Korea 8-0 to finish the Asian Champions Trophy league stage unbeaten with 15 points from five wins. Dilpreet Singh scored twice, while six others found the net. India will face South Korea again in Wednesday's semifinal in Mohali, while Japan take on Malaysia in the other last-four clash.

title: Murdered Punjab anti-drug activist's kin seeks 'distance' from Indira Gandhi family
content: Bhim Singh, father of the slain anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh Jhota, requested certain political figures to stay away from a protest. Singh expressed his concerns regarding the presence of Rahul Gandhi and the family of Beant Singh. He emphasized the ongoing tensions within the Sikh community towards the legacy of Indira Gandhi. Additionally, Singh criticized local MLA Vijay Singla for his comments on the protest's impact on business.

title: Cyclone Murasu to make landfall near at Andhra coast tonight; 120 kmph winds expected
content: Cyclone Murasu has intensified and is predicted to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast soon. It is expected to bring strong winds reaching up to 120 kmph and heavy rainfall. Several districts in Andhra Pradesh will experience severe weather conditions due to the cyclone. Precautionary measures have been implemented, including rescue operations and evacuation arrangements. Fishermen have been advised to avoid venturing into the sea during this period.

title: No election for IOA Athletes’ Commission as all 10 candidates declared unopposed
content: The IOA Athletes’ Commission election scheduled for November 3 has been deemed unnecessary after all 10 candidates were declared elected unopposed. The withdrawal of nominations by Kidambi Srikanth and Sudha Singh left one candidate for each position. The Commission will comprise five men and five women representing nine sports.

title: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports
content: The government is addressing a dispute regarding reduced import duties on bulk Scotch whisky imports. Liquor industry executives were assured that these imports qualify for the 75 percent duty reduction. The disagreement arose after tax officials questioned the eligibility of bulk shipments under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement. Major liquor companies, including Diageo and Pernod Ricard, have been affected by this dispute.

title: GRAP-2 curbs imposed in Delhi as AQI hits ‘very poor’ category at 324
content: Delhi’s air quality slipped to ‘very poor’ for the first time this season, with AQI at 324, the highest in nine months. CAQM invoked GRAP Stage 2, while vehicle checks at borders caused long jams. The High Court refused to stay curbs on non-BS-VI vehicles, and the Supreme Court allowed certified green crackers for two days before Diwali.

title: 'Sometimes you've got to wait': Zverev becomes oldest first-time No. 1 in 52 years
content: For the first time, Alexander Zverev has ascended to the world No. 1 ranking, marking a significant achievement in his career. This impressive feat comes on the heels of his triumphs at the French Open and US Open. His rise to the top occurred after Jannik Sinner, the previous holder of the title, decided to conclude his season.

title: Delhi HC stays JNU professor Bimol Akoijam's termination over sexual harassment case
content: In a significant legal development, the Delhi high court has intervened to temporarily suspend the termination of Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam. Facing sexual harassment allegations from 11 female students filed in May, Akoijam has refuted the claims and is appealing his dismissal from October 9. An internal committee had suggested disciplinary measures after its investigation.

title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 polls?
content: Akhilesh Yadav's recent visit to Azam Khan in jail underscores their deep political connection amidst ongoing legal troubles. Following Azam's fleeting bail, the Enforcement Directorate swiftly took him back into custody, adding complexity to the Samajwadi Party's election preparations. Balancing support for Azam while appealing to Muslim constituents presents a significant challenge for Akhilesh as he navigates potential electoral repercussions.

title: Naman Dhir makes his mark on maiden overseas tour, wins India's Impact Player medal
content: In the recent T20I series against New Zealand, Naman Dhir showcased his prowess, garnering the Impact Player of the Series accolade. Scoring 138 runs over five matches, he significantly contributed to India's early victories. His performance in the middle order underscored his importance, even with just two overs bowled. Now, with the T20I series behind them, India looks forward to the impending ODI matches.

title: '3 crore Bangladeshi infiltrators': Amit Shah counters Rahul's anti-SIR pitch
content: In a verbal blitzkrieg, a day after Rahul's mega Ramlila Maidan rally in the national capital, Shah said that behind the Congress's criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) lies an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", three crore of whom, he claimed, were struck off the electoral rolls during the revision.

title: Abhishek, Sooryavanshi feature in Tilak-led India A squad for Rising Stars Asia Cup
content: BCCI has announced a strong 15-member India A squad for the upcoming ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup. The tournament will take place in Doha, Qatar, from November 19 to 29, featuring several promising players. Tilak Varma will captain the squad, with Rajat Patidar as his deputy for the competition. India A is placed in Group B alongside Pakistan A, Nepal, and UAE for the group stage.

title: Iran calls US biggest threat to NPT, warns of stronger defence push
content: Esmail Baghaei, spokesperson for the Iranian foreign ministry, has branded the United States as the foremost danger to global nuclear non-proliferation. He raised alarms over military threats from the U.S., which he claims undermine the Non-Proliferation Treaty. Amid ongoing pressures, Iran's discussions about its nuclear policy have intensified, yet the country remains steadfast in honoring its nuclear commitments, maintaining a peaceful program that has been validated repeatedly.

title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
content: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda

content: The employees, aged 60 and above, were asked to discontinue service from November. They alleged that they had been treated unfairly and their services terminated without proper notice.

content: During the raid, the accused were allegedly found storing medicines and pharmaceutical drugs without valid licences, permits or authorisations and replacing labels on the stored medicines.

content: Inaugurating a Kisan Mahapanchayat at Plachimada in Keralam’s Palakkad, Charuni says the agreement will allow unrestricted imports and affect not only agriculture but also small businesses, fisheries, poultry farming and the dairy sector

title: VMC Commissioner calls for smooth, transparent vote counting for ULB elections

title: Directorate General of Civil Aviation probe into Belagavi trainer aircraft forced landing case finds many deficiencies in training academy
content: On May 30, 2023, a 24-year-old student trainee pilot flying a TECNAM P2008JC aircraft was involved in a forced landing incident near Belagavi Airport while conducting a solo circuit and landing exercise.

content: The digitisation move has been planned to make the process of obtaining TDR more transparent and reduce delays, and facilitate faster land acquisition for road widening and other infrastructure projects.

content: The proposed service is primarily oriented towards leisure and tourism traffic between the three destinations, supplemented by the potential for general passenger movement

content: The ship, which completed the voyage spanning over 22,000 nautical miles across the oceans, was honoured with a water cannon salute and a ceremonial welcome by the Naval Band.

content: A total of 4,628 emergency beds, 205 relief camps and 807 ambulances and mobile medical units kept ready; 1,103 pregnant women shifted to nearby hospitals

content: haley Stevens lost a bitter party primary (inner party election) to progressive Abdul El-Sayed . the immediate political damage is difficult to quantify, but the optics and the timing – coming just when many polls are showing a Republican rout – could hardly be worse for Democrats .

content: According to data from the US Department of Homeland Security's SEVIS, the number of active international student records in the US fell by 7.07 per cent in October 2026 compared with October 2025.

content: The Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, aim to strengthen consumer protection through faster complaint resolution, round-the-clock customer support and greater accountability of service providers.

content: The GRAP-II involves a series of restrictions that include mechanical or vacuum sweeping of roads and water sprinkling, raising parking fees to discourage the use of personal vehicles, increasing the frequency of Metro services and CNG and electric buses.

content: suspected cyberattack targeted supermarket refrigeration systems . supermarket chains including Delhaize and Carrefour in Belgium, ICA and Coop in Sweden and SuperValu in Ireland have been affected . the attacks are a deliberate attempt to disrupt the europe's food supply .
